page_title: REST Servers in Go: Part 6 - authentication

summary.title: REST Servers in Go: Part 6 - authentication
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add HTTPS and HTTP basic authentication to a Go REST server, including bcrypt password verification and per-path auth middleware.
keywords: how to secure a rest api in go
takeaways: Use TLS/HTTPS as the foundation; HTTP basic auth is considered safe only over HTTPS.
Go's net/http provides Request.BasicAuth; respond with 401 and a WWW-Authenticate header when verification fails.
Store only bcrypt hashes of passwords, never plaintext; bcrypt adds salting, timing-attack resistance and deliberate slowness.
Apply authentication middleware to specific Gorilla mux routes, such as only the POST /task/ path, rather than all paths.
summary.summary: The post explains the difference between authentication and authorization, then argues that TLS should underpin any auth scheme. It builds a small Go HTTPS server that protects a path with HTTP basic auth, verifying passwords against bcrypt hashes, and tests it with curl and a Go client. It then retrofits the task store server from earlier parts with a BasicAuth middleware applied to a single route. The author closes with trade-offs, noting tokens and OAuth as alternatives and recommending a security expert for critical systems.
